fit: freeze-dried cranberry powder and baseline PHQ-9 screening in healthy older adults
assessment: The protocol scheduled PHQ-9, and the Connell thesis and paper confirm baseline PHQ-9 screening in COMBAT participants. The cognitive, metabolite and baseline analyses do not give a post-treatment depression comparison by arm. Same trial family as ISRCTN76069316.

fit: cranberry drink and HADS depression in healthy students
assessment: Overall HADS depression p = .98 and treatment-by-visit p = .70. The distinct adjusted week-12 difference was −0.404 points, 95% CI −1.88 to 1.08, p = .59. Publication n = 72 and registry n = 64 remain unreconciled.

fit: ginger rhizome powder and Hamilton anxiety with concurrent SSRI use
assessment: The publisher abstract explicitly identifies IRCT20201108049306N1 and reports increased active-arm scores while concluding anxiety decreased. The registered powder, SSRIs and Hamilton measures do not resolve the direction without the original tables or a correction.

fit: anxiety outcomes in a Parkinson formula trial with unresolved ingredients
assessment: The official abstract reports Hamilton and self-rated anxiety differences. Publisher metadata identifies legacy PDF record 8908, which was unavailable. Ginger, formula composition and numerical outcomes remain unverified.

fit: standardized ginger root powder and a secondary anxiety outcome in healthy adults
assessment: The original manuscript and indexed journal table give DASS-21 anxiety median change −1 versus 0, Mann–Whitney U = 286, p = .511 in the thesis and .51 rounded in the journal. Low baseline scores, a short study, and healthy adults limit the comparison.
